message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 17 November 2026 23:40 to 18 November 2026 23:40 UTC (19 November run date in Asia/Kolkata).
**Scope:** Products.txt and List_of_SIA_Completed.txt, combined with obvious duplicates normalized, plus the dedicated MongoDB ecosystem sweep. Product presence and installed versions have not been independently verified.

New, relevant advisories were found for NGINX and OpenJDK/Oracle Java. Prioritize review of exposed installations and verify actual versions and configurations.

### NGINX: five memory-corruption vulnerabilities
**CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634 and CVE-2026-113425.** F5 rates each high (CVSS 3.1: 8.1) and critical (CVSS 4.0: 9.2); nginx.org uses different severity labels. Depending on the issue and configuration, unauthenticated attackers may corrupt memory, crash a worker or execute code with worker privileges. The issues affect HTTP/2, HTTP/3, resolver or mail-proxy configurations respectively. NGINX is explicitly listed in the inventory; affected version ranges differ. CERT-EU published its advisory on 18 November. [CERT-EU advisory](https://www.cert.europa.eu/publications/security-advisories/2026-022/) | [NGINX advisories and affected versions](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html).

### NGINX: TLS request-body denial of service
**CVE-2026-118899.** NGINX rates this major; F5 rates it high, CVSS 3.1 7.5. An infinite loop while reading a TLS 1.3 request body can stall a worker process. NGINX is listed; the vendor identifies affected versions 1.13.0 through 1.31.8 and fixed releases 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. This was among the NGINX disclosures reported on 18 November. [NGINX advisory index](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html) | [Cloudflare analysis](https://radar.cloudflare.com/zero-wire/nginx2root).

### OpenJDK and Oracle Java: CVE-2026-114938
**Severity:** High, CVSS 3.1 8.1 according to Oracle; Red Hat rates its impact critical. A Base64 decoder memory-corruption flaw can permit code execution or a crash when an affected application processes attacker-supplied input on x86-64 hardware supporting AVX-512 VBMI. OpenJDK and Oracle Java are listed, including Java 17; affected builds and vendor distributions must be checked. Cisco and Adoptium issued further advisories on 18 November; the original disclosure was 17 November. [Adoptium guidance](https://adoptium.net/news/2026/11/temurin-november-2026-cspu-java4shell/) | [Cisco advisory](https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nov2026-java-rce-eCa6ss9z).

### MongoDB ecosystem
The dedicated sweep considered Server and editions, mongod/mongos, Atlas and related services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, tools, operators, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, integrations and MongoDB-owned libraries, including advisories without MongoDB in the title. Searches included MongoDB alerts, CVE/NVD, GitHub advisories, CISA and security research. No new in-window MongoDB ecosystem vulnerability was verified. MongoDB's [CVE-2026-118383 announcement](https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/important-mongodb-security-update-available-action-required-november-10-2026/344843) is dated 10 November and is not counted as new; [Percona's 18 November release](https://docs.percona.com/new/2026/11/18/percona-server-for-mongodb-8317-5-has-been-released/) mentions upstream fixes but does not establish a new MongoDB disclosure.

**Closing:** Prompt review is recommended for affected NGINX and Java deployments, especially internet-facing systems. The large inventory includes ambiguous entries such as “F”, “Carbon”, “SIP” and “Blackbox CLI”, and inconsistent or missing versions; these were not treated as confidently identified products. Search coverage is limited and no finding does not establish safety.
